children: ASOS shares fell sharply after the London-listed online retailer suffered a cyber incident that may have exposed some customer names and contact details.
The company said it was investigating activity involving third-party platforms that it uses to communicate with customers after an unauthorized notification was sent out to customers Tuesday morning.
ASOS said it was too early to quantify any potential impact on trading. Shares in London fell more than 10%.
"We took immediate action to restrict access to the notification platforms and are working with our internal and external specialist advisers, as well as all relevant authorities," the group said.
The company said basic customer information such as names and contact details may have been accessed, but that it believed no payment-card information or account passwords had been affected.
ASOS said its website and app were operating as normal.
